problem.title: RabbitMQ Unbounded Queue Length Exhausting RAM and Thrashing to Disk
problem.prompt: RabbitMQ queue without length limits accumulating messages during a consumer outage.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Every message queue must enforce bounded maximum length or byte quotas to prevent unconstrained memory and disk exhaustion."
Production Hardening: Set queue policies: 'x-max-length' or 'x-max-length-bytes' with 'x-overflow: reject-publish' or 'drop-head', or route overflow messages to a dead-letter exchange (DLX).
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.
constraints: Incident Scenario Baseline: RabbitMQ queue without length limits accumulating messages during a consumer outage.
Failure Cascade Path: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze
Sub-millisecond rejection / shed latency for overloaded requests

stages.learnerPrompt: Compare naive architecture vs production-hardened patterns. Walk through the key trade-offs and operational attributes.

referenceMaterial.summary: Architectural comparison of naive unconstrained allocations versus production-hardened mechanical sympathy.
tradeOffs: Ingress Admission: Naive unconstrained buffering causes queue bloat and GC exhaustion. Mitigation: Bounded ingress gate with fast non-blocking shedding.
Resource Strategy: Static capacity allocations collapse under brownouts. Mitigation: Dynamic adaptive limits scaling to real-time physical bounds.
Outage Impact: Cascading lock convoys and memory saturation. Mitigation: Isolated failure domains keep P99 latency flat and protected.
alternatives: Naive Approach: Queue accumulates 10 million messages in RAM. RabbitMQ begins paging messages to disk, slowing throughput to a crawl and blocking incoming connections
Production-Hardened Pattern: Set queue policies: 'x-max-length' or 'x-max-length-bytes' with 'x-overflow: reject-publish' or 'drop-head', or route overflow messages to a dead-lett

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Queue accumulates 10 million messages in RAM. RabbitMQ begins paging messages to disk, slowing throughput to a crawl and blocking incoming connections, bringing the entire messaging infrastructure down.
Breakdown Chain: 50k Mut. → Row X-Lock → Spinlock Thrash → Deadlock Graph → 💥 DB Freeze
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.
